title: The readout, annotated
direction: A×C · Round 8 · /reports · DS (document specimen), the page's one paper moment
summary: Replaces the two invented case dossiers (six metrics, client profiles, 2026 windows) with the one thing Kelwin can honestly show: the readout itself, whole, as a ruled sheet that pairs each section's format with one example written to show it, the audit's four parts bracketed in the left margin, and an editor's note in the right margin giving the standard each annotated section is held to.
story: The signature beat and the answer to “can I see a real one?”: not yet, so here is exactly what one is. The lede reconciles the count once (six sections: the constraint first, the audit's four parts, the next step) and the margin dimension repeats the band's “The four parts”. Read top to bottom it is the audit's argument in order: the constraint named in one sentence (underlined in red, as on the band's page one), the narrative, the channels and where they leak, what nobody measures, the order to fix it in, and the line every readout ends on.

reference.site: Wispr Flow (editor's annotations set over the text they mark) · Notion customer stories (numbered sections read down a page)
reference.borrowed: Annotations that sit beside the copy they mark and explain why it is written that way, so the reader sees the document and the editor's standard at once.
reference.kelwin: No floating pills or photo: a 1px-ruled paper sheet on the 12-column grid (cols 2–9), each section a table row (format left, example right under an Example chip). Right margin (cols 10–12): four editor's notes tied to the sheet's edge by leaders at their section's title, each a standard rather than a restatement. Left margin (col 1): the kit's dimension, vertical, bracketing sections 02–05 as “The four parts”, the band's own measure. The examples are drawn in type and rules, never as charts or numbers. The one red is the editor's underline under the constraint.

motion: entrance (the page's first body moment): the sheet fades in, its column heads appear, then the six section rules draw top to bottom (180ms apart) with each row typeset after its rule; the four-parts dimension builds down the left margin with rows 02–05 (each segment rides its row's rise); the four editor's notes draw their leaders out into the margin and fade in; the red underline inks under the constraint last (about 3.6s).
ambient: none; the sheet is still once typeset.
on the live site: plays once when the sheet is 40% visible. Reduced motion: the typeset sheet at once.

phone: ≤1279: the sheet widens to cols 1–9, the notes keep cols 10–12, and the margin dimension goes (the lede names the four parts at every width). ≤1023: the sheet takes the full width; each editor's note drops in under its section's format line (a short leader, then the note); the channel map stacks channel over trigger with the route beside them; the gap report stacks its three groups; the four quarters sit two by two. ≤767: one column per section (index and title, format, note, then the example indented under the title); the four voices put the speaker over the sentence; the four quarters become a short vertical list with the first square filled. No content is hidden at any width.
notes: A reading surface: ≈2,200px at 1440, over the 1,400 cap by design (the brief allows reading surfaces to run long; cropping it would hide the format the page exists to show). The doc is the kit's .ac-doc on the paper section; the SpecimenTag is the kit's. One red element: the underline — the same mark as the band's page one, a deliberate thread (see reports-head notes). At ≥1024 the four quarters share subgrid rows, so every “Needs” sits on one line however the steps wrap; the gap items are balanced so none strands a word. The margin dimension hangs off each row's key cell (position: relative) and is never animated on its own: Chromium skips painting a filled animation on an absolutely positioned piece that lies outside its row's box (production must keep this). Nothing in it is a figure: no numbers beyond section indexes and quarter labels.
